items.question: How was the March 2025 Spicy Lady casualty categorized, and in which waterway and near what landmark did it take place?
items.expected_answer: It was categorized as a fire/explosion, occurring in Chatham Strait about 1 mile west of Point Gardner, Alaska.

evidence.quote: February 4, 2026 MIR-26-04 Fire aboard Fishing Vessel Spicy Lady MIR-26-04 2 Casualty Summary Casualty type Fire/Explosion Location Chatham Strait, about 1 mile west of Point Gardner, Alaska

items.notes: Tests retrieval of the casualty summary table header rows, which sit right after a page break; the only summary-table boundary available spans the page header.

items.question: Why were investigators unable to pin down what started the blaze on the fishing vessel Spicy Lady?
items.expected_answer: Several possible ignition sources existed in the forward berthing area (wiring, electrical components and lithium-ion batteries); the arcing and corrosion found on the wires may have occurred after the fire started or during firefighting, and because of severe damage and the space being unoccupied, investigators could not tell when or why the bag of lithium-ion batteries ignited, so the probable cause was an unknown source on a bunk.

evidence.quote: Possible ignition sources in the forward berthing area included electrical wiring, electrical components, and the lithium-ion batteries stored in the portside bunk (some of which the captain said were charging at the time).
investigators were unable to determine when this occurred in the ignition sequence, and it is possible that the arcing and corrosion occurred after the initial fire or during firefighting efforts.

due to severe fire damage in the berthing area, and because the space was unoccupied when the fire started, investigators were unable to determine when the bag containing the lithium-ion batteries caught fire or what caused it to ignite.

items.notes: Tests combining the analysis reasons why the ignition source stayed undetermined.
